retirement_preconditions: replacement is bound and active
old ciphertext reconciliation completed
old encrypted-record dependency count is zero
concerns.recovery: Interrupted reconciliation keeps the previous key retained; stale-key writes and downgrade remain fail-closed.

retirement_preconditions: version is not active
live encrypted-record dependency count is zero
idempotency dependency count is zero
live refresh-lease dependency count is zero
concerns.recovery: Unknown, missing or ambiguous version metadata fails closed; raw handles or idempotency keys are never persisted to make rotation easier.

retirement_preconditions: resolver accepts replacement key id
control-plane signer emits replacement key id
staging traffic verifies on replacement
no accepted caller still requires legacy-v1 or previous key id
concerns.recovery: Keep the previous accepted key during failed cutover; unknown/revoked key ids, replay and stale requests fail closed.

retirement_preconditions: replacement is retained before switch
explicit active version is switched only after keyring validation
encrypted contact rows no longer depend on the retired encryption version
lookup rows no longer depend on the retired lookup version
concerns.recovery: A failed switch retains the previous versions; implicit JSON-array ordering is not an accepted active-key authority.

concerns.provider_identity: R2 API token -> Access Key ID + Secret Access Key
retirement_preconditions: replacement token is scoped to the intended account and bucket
replacement Access Key ID and Secret Access Key are bound as one pair
bounded staging R2 access succeeds with replacement
Worker binding metadata verifies replacement before old token revocation
concerns.recovery: Keep the previous R2 token valid until replacement verification; routine code promotion never rotates or rebinds this pair.

concerns.provider_constraint: Do not assume old and replacement client secrets remain simultaneously valid for the exact Google OAuth registration type. A classic secret reset can invalidate the old secret immediately; exact provider capability must be discovered before mutation.
retirement_preconditions: replacement credential is issued by the authoritative Google application owner
resolver binding is prepared before any destructive reset where provider semantics require it
staging authorization-code/token exchange verifies the replacement without secret readback
provider rejection maps to safe operator/re-auth state rather than a second OAuth state machine
concerns.recovery: If overlap is unavailable, use a controlled cutover with explicit maintenance/re-auth handling; never revoke/reset first and hope routine deployment repairs the binding.

concerns.provider_constraint: Microsoft Entra application password credentials support add-before-remove; bind and verify the replacement credential before removing the previous password credential by key id.
retirement_preconditions: replacement password credential is added to the intended application registration
resolver binding is switched to replacement
staging authorization-code/token exchange verifies replacement without secret readback
previous password credential is removed only after replacement verification
concerns.recovery: If replacement verification fails, keep the previous password credential valid and restore the prior resolver binding; user refresh-token lifecycle remains AR-8A authority.
